subject: ophthalmology
title: Anterior uveitis

steps.tx: **Acute anterior uveitis** strikes one red painful photophobic eye with circumcorneal injection, cells and flare in the anterior chamber, keratic precipitates on endothelium, miosis and low or high pressure. **Granulomatous** disease (sarcoid, TB, sympathetic ophthalmia) lays large mutton fat precipitates with iris nodules (Koeppe at pupil margin, Busacca in stroma), while **nongranulomatous** HLA-B27-associated attacks (ankylosing spondylitis, Reiter, IBD, psoriasis) shower fine precipitates with fibrin and hypopyon. Slit lamp grading of cells and flare stages severity and treatment response.
steps.say: Red painful eye with cells floating inside: anterior uveitis. Big greasy precipitates mean granulomatous.

vis.alt: Slit lamp view showing circumcorneal injection, anterior chamber cells and flare, fine and mutton fat keratic precipitates, and iris nodules (Koeppe, Busacca) characteristic of anterior uveitis.
vis.caption: Key clinical signs of acute anterior uveitis, distinguishing granulomatous and non-granulomatous forms. Image: Yedoct, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Systemic hunt follows pattern: unilateral alternating attacks suggest seronegative spondyloarthropathy (sacroiliac imaging, HLA-B27); bilateral granulomatous disease seeks sarcoidosis (chest imaging, ACE), tuberculosis (Mantoux or interferon assay), syphilis serology and herpetic causes (raised pressure with iris atrophy). Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis (heterochromia, stellate precipitates, cataract and glaucoma without synechiae) and Posner Schlossman glaucomatocyclitic crises (recurrent pressure spikes with mild cells) are unilateral special patterns. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis causes silent chronic bilateral disease needing screening.
steps.say: Alternating red eyes with back pain: HLA-B27. Quiet white eyes in arthritic children still need screening.

steps.tx: Treatment pairs intensive **topical steroids** (prednisolone hourly in severe attacks, tapering by cells) with **cycloplegic mydriatics** (atropine or homatropine breaking and preventing posterior synechiae while easing ciliary spasm pain). Raised pressure gets aqueous suppressants; herpetic disease adds oral antivirals; systemic steroids or immunosuppression (methotrexate, azathioprine, biologics) control posterior involvement, bilateral or recurrent disease. Dark glasses, rest and compliance counselling bridge the painful weeks. Steroid responders and cataract complicate prolonged drops.
steps.say: Steroid drops plus dilating drops is the anterior uveitis pair. Dilatation stops iris sticking to lens.

steps.tx: Complications punish delay: posterior synechiae (iris stuck to lens, irregular pupil, seclusio and angle closure), peripheral anterior synechiae, complicated cataract, secondary glaucoma (inflammatory, steroid induced or synechial), cystoid macular oedema, hypotony with phthisis in burnt out ciliary shutdown, and band keratopathy in chronic childhood disease. **Endophthalmitis** (postoperative or post traumatic with pain, lid swelling, hypopyon and vitritis) is the emergency mimic needing intravitreal antibiotics and vitrectomy, never steroids alone. Sympathetic ophthalmia threatens the fellow eye after penetrating injury.
steps.say: Iris glued to lens plus rising pressure is synechial angle closure. Postoperative pus inside the eye is endophthalmitis: inject antibiotics.
